saints.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The “Angelic Doctor,” Dominican friar whose Summa Theologiae joined faith and reason so profoundly that the Church has held him up as a master of theology…
biography: Born about 1225 at the castle of Roccasecca near Aquino, Thomas was schooled from the age of five at Monte Cassino and then at Naples, where he joined the Order of Preachers. His family held him prisoner for nearly a year to break his resolve, but won free in 1244 to study under Albert the Great at Paris and Cologne.

He taught at Paris, Orvieto, Rome, and Naples, composing for Urban IV the office of Corpus Christi with its hymns. His Summa contra Gentiles and the unfinished Summa Theologiae joined the newly recovered philosophy of Aristotle to Christian doctrine with unmatched order and depth.

On 6 December 1273, after a vision during Mass at Naples, he wrote no more, saying that all he had written seemed like straw. Summoned by Gregory X to the Council of Lyons, he died on the way at the Cistercian abbey of Fossanova on 7 March 1274.

He was canonized by John XXII in 1323 and declared a Doctor of the Church by Pius V in 1567. His relics were carried to Toulouse on 28 January 1369, the day of his present feast, and in 1880 Leo XIII named him patron of all Catholic schools.
saints.knownFor: The synthesis of faith and reason; the Summa Theologiae; Eucharistic hymns such as the Pange Lingua.

canonization.canonized: 1323 by Pope John XXII; declared a Doctor of the Church in 1567 by Pope St. Pius V
